probeMissions: BASE, common to every mission below: `node dist/cli.js init --yes --example` (runward 0.36.0, the request-triage reference mission) into an empty directory, which is green under `check --strict` (measured: exit 0). Then `node dist/cli.js check --strict --freeze` on it, which seals 18 evidence files into runward/evidence-lock.json — 11 files the manifests cite as applied evidence plus the 5 gated manifests and 2 more cited documents. That sealed tree is `m/seal`: exit 0, seal present, count 18, 0 violations. Every tampered mission is a full copy of it with exactly one thing changed. Builders kept at tools/make-missions.mjs, tools/make-freeze-missions.mjs, tools/make-extra-missions.mjs, tools/make-lock-shapes.mjs.

WRITE-SIDE missions (`check --freeze` and `check --attest`), each an unsealed copy of the base tree: f-plain, which freezes to exactly the 18-file lock, 2022 bytes, keys sorted, trailing newline present. f-bracket, which adds two house rules whose ids separate the three anchorings of `/^\[.*\]$/` — `a[b]` (contains `[`, ends with `]`, does NOT start with `[`) and `[a]b` (starts with `[`, contains `]`, does NOT end with `]`) — each `impact: LOW` so corpus divergence does not report them (an unwritten rule is only 'extra' at CRITICAL/HIGH on a gated phase), each with an `applied` row appended to the RULE CONFORMANCE table of runward/floor.md citing a file nothing else in the mission cites (code/probe-ab.ts, code/probe-ba.ts). Pristine: exit 0, `sealed 20 evidence file(s)`, both probe files in the lock. A first attempt appended the rows below the wrong table and sealed 18, which is why the row position is part of the recipe. f-unreadable was built and DISCARDED: a cited unreadable file reddens the gate with 8 EACCES conformance gaps, and `--freeze` refuses a red gate, so the write side cannot be reached that way — hence t-attest-unreadable instead.
